title: The Case for the Creation of an AI Threat Fusion Center
gist: An Insider episode note: Rebecca Hersman argues the United States should stand up a dedicated AI Threat Fusion Center, on the logic that as AI systems grow more sophisticated so do the threats nefarious actors can mount, and that the upfront cost is justified over the long run.

themes.theme: Proposal for a U.S. AI Threat Fusion Center

insights.claim: The United States should create a dedicated AI Threat Fusion Center to consolidate assessment of artificial-intelligence-enabled threats.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Signals a new institutional line of US AI-security spending — relevant to government-facing AI security, threat-intel and evaluation vendors.

insights.claim: As artificial-intelligence systems become more sophisticated, the sophistication of threats available to nefarious actors rises in parallel.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Offensive AI capability scales with frontier capability, so security budgets should be indexed to model progress rather than to past incident counts.

insights.claim: The upfront cost of building a standing AI threat-assessment institution is worth paying because the long-run payoff exceeds it.
